video.title: We Copied His $10K+/Month Business From Scratch in a New City

summary: Chris Koerner and Kyler (22, Utah) replicate Kyler's Facebook Marketplace washer/dryer rental business from scratch in Dallas-Fort Worth, a market saturated after their earlier viral video. They skip name, LLC and website, post a $60/month listing, boost it for $20, buy a cheap set at a garage sale for $125, and deliver and install. In one afternoon they rent two sets for $70/month recurring in about 4 hours of work. They argue competition grows the market, a $20 boost can acquire a customer worth around $1,300, and the bottleneck is the owner's time. Revenue extrapolations are hypothetical and promotional (Koerner sells a membership).

ideas.name: Washer and dryer rentals via Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Buy used washer/dryer sets cheaply, rent them monthly to renters via Facebook Marketplace listings, with free delivery, install and repairs.
ideas.business_model: Monthly recurring rental, with an option to sell units
ideas.customer: Renters in apartments or homes with laundry hookups but no machines; people who avoid laundromats or buying
ideas.problem: Buying, maintaining and moving a washer and dryer is a headache, and laundromats are inconvenient
ideas.offer: Washer and dryer rental at about $60-85/month for a set, delivery, install and free repairs, 6 or 12 month minimum

pricing.model: Monthly rental, set or single unit
pricing.notes: Competitor listings were $50-85. Boosted posts can justify a higher price (e.g. $70 to $85). Single units are priced above half the set price.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace listing with clear outdoor photo, category 'washer and dryer sets', 'free delivery, install and maintenance' description, priced $60. Boost for $1-2/day or $20 for a 1-day boost to reach the top of results.

quote.text: you can boost the post for $1 to $2 a day, which isn't very much money, but it'll put your listing to the top of the marketplace results
quote.speaker: Kyler

acquisition_channels.details: Suggested joining local Dallas buy/sell groups as a differentiator; not yet done.
Customers whose dryer breaks call to rent one; install visits yield contacts and free used machines.
Idea to talk to property managers and use door hangers at complexes with hookups but no machines.

ideas.delivery: Operator sources used sets from Facebook Marketplace or garage sales, rents a truck, delivers and installs with new hoses and gaskets (channel locks needed), tests the units, and handles repairs. Installs take about 20 minutes. Owner does everything physically.
unit_economics_claims: Set bought for $125, rents at $60-70/month, profitable after month 2
$20 boost acquired a customer worth about $1,300 over 2 years
Two rentals ($70/month) from about 4 hours of work in Dallas
ideas.startup_cost: Roughly $125-300 per set, plus truck rental $29.99/day (Hertz, no mileage), about $15 channel locks, new hoses, optional $20 boost. Name, LLC, logo, website and insurance skipped.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Same day in Dallas demonstration; two sets rented in about 3-4 hours

acquisition.how: Marketplace listing and boosts can be templated and scheduled; AI can draft listings and reply to inquiries, but Facebook automation limits and ToS apply.

onboarding.how: Agents can handle chat, scheduling and collecting a phone number and address, but contracts and payments need setup and ghosting needs follow-up.

delivery.how: Physical sourcing, transport, installation and repairs must be done by a person every time.

billing.how: Recurring card billing via Stripe-type tools could be automated; transcript does not state how billing is done.

support.how: Agents can triage messages, but leaks, breakdowns and repairs need a visit.

uk_applicability.notes: Appliance rental works in the UK (Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree exist), but many UK rentals include appliances, sets are often combined washer-dryers or freestanding with different hookups, vans are needed, and electrical safety (PAT testing) and consumer rental terms apply. Fewer unfurnished renters lack washers. Hertz-style no-mileage van hire is common.

risks: Competition from copycats after a viral video
Leaks causing water damage liability, insurance skipped in demo
Physical work limits scale to owner's time

tactics.name: Post first, buy after demand
steps: Publish the Facebook Marketplace rental listing first
Wait for a client
Then source the washer/dryer set
Check local price range of sets beforehand

quote.text: we first publish the listing, wait for a client, and then we will buy the washer and dryer set
quote.speaker: Kyler

tactics.name: Boost listings for visibility and price up
steps: Boost the approved listing for $1-2/day or a $20 1-day boost
Raise price when boosting (e.g. $70 to $85)
Respond first, since pricing is similar across competitors

tactics.name: Source cheap sets
steps: Look for garage-sale posts, which skip individual listings
Target $100-200, older direct-drive sets with agitator
Avoid Samsung
Skip units with noise problems (bearing)
Message 5-6 sellers and confirm you can pick up today
Prefer clean units needing no work

tactics.name: Rent a truck to prove demand
steps: Rent from Hertz, Avis or National at about $30/day with no mileage charge
Avoid Home Depot/U-Haul per-mile fees
Once demand proven, buy or lease a cheap truck

tactics.name: Install checklist
steps: Always use new hoses with new gaskets
Test heating and hot water and balance the unit
Show customer the lint trap
State clearly that building plumbing is not your responsibility
Get a phone number before delivering

tactics.name: Relentless follow-up on leads
steps: Follow up about seven times
Drive to the complex even if ghosted
Knock doors if no unit number, since each customer is worth $700/year

quote.text: if he doesn't follow up like seven times like an obsessive girlfriend, he's not going to respond.

warnings.warning: Reusing old hoses risks leaks and flooding calls; use new hoses and gaskets.
Avoid Samsung machines; avoid non-direct-drive units with control boards if you want reliability.
Clarify that building plumbing leaks are the property's responsibility.
The truck-rental approach is only for proving demand, not long term.

lessons.lesson: Competition can enlarge the market: awareness from many listings creates customers who weren't searching.

quote.text: That increases the awareness, right? Because you said there's like 60 listings in DFW right now
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: When prices are similar, the first responsive, honest seller who delivers wins.
Test demand before spending on branding or incorporation: skip name, LLC and website at first.
Frame ad spend by lifetime value: $20 to acquire a roughly $1,300 customer is a strong return.
Persistent follow-up is required to close; most leads need several touches.
Physical delivery-based businesses are limited by owner time, not demand.
Trade-ins from customers give free inventory, compounding recurring revenue.
Hourly-rate extrapolations from a single day of sign-ups overstate profit because they ignore churn, repairs, insurance and sourcing time.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand live demonstration with some concrete numbers (set cost, price, boost, inquiries), but results come from one afternoon and the headline income projections are hypothetical extrapolations. Prior $10K/month claim is unverified here.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes TK Owners membership; Kyler promotes his own coaching/contracts and YouTube channel.
